diff.text: public static bool TryParseAutolink(StringLineGroup text, out string link, out bool isEmail)
// An absolute URI, for these purposes, consists of a scheme followed by a colon (:)
// followed by zero or more characters other than ASCII whitespace and control characters, <, and >.
// If the URI includes these characters, they must be percent-encoded (e.g. %20 for a space).
// a scheme is any sequence of 2–32 characters
// and followed by any combination of ASCII letters, digits, or the symbols plus (”+”), period (”.”), or hyphen (”-”).
// An email address, for these purposes, is anything that matches the non-normative regex from the HTML5 spec:

reasons.detail: Scheme length check rejects valid 2-char schemes (builder.Length <=2) and email domain validation never updates pc, so consecutive dots/hyphen-dot and empty labels are incorrectly accepted.

diff.text: // We may have an email char?

reasons.detail: Off-by-one rejects valid 2-char schemes (check is builder.Length <=2 instead of <2) and scheme length >32 check is gated on state>0 so never fires while scanning scheme, so overly long schemes are accepted; e.g., <ab:foo> incorrectly fails.

diff.text: // Chars valid for both scheme and email
// If this is not a special char valid also for url scheme, then we have an email

reasons.detail: Scheme length 2-32 not enforced in scored loop: upper limit only checked when state>0 so a long alphanumeric prefix (state==0) can exceed 32 chars then hit ':' and pass, and lower bound uses <=2 rejecting valid 2-char schemes.

diff.text: // a scheme is any sequence of 2–32 characters

reasons.detail: Marked loop rejects valid 2-char schemes (builder.Length <=2 should be <2) and the 32-char limit is dead code because state>0 is never true before ':' is seen, so overlong schemes are not rejected as intended.
Logic-heavy change in source file; Spark Open rated it 5%.

pc is never updated so consecutive-dot/hyphen-dot check is dead, and hasMinus is assigned only on '-' and never cleared on alphanumeric so valid hyphenated domains like a-b are incorrectly rejected and invalid ones may be accepted.

diff.text: // An absolute URI, for these purposes, consists of a scheme followed by a colon (:)
// followed by zero or more characters other than ASCII whitespace and control characters, <, and >.
// If the URI includes these characters, they must be percent-encoded (e.g. %20 for a space).

reasons.detail: pc is initialized to '\0' and never assigned (pc = c missing), so the check if (pc=='.'||pc=='-') is dead code; email domains with '..' or '.-' are incorrectly accepted instead of rejected.

Unconditional debug logging Log.WriteLine/DumpTo will crash when Log is null and breaks output, and the InsertAfter closed-container path was removed while the new nextInline==null branch incorrectly rewrites inlineState.Inline which can misplace/duplicate inlines.

Logic-heavy change in source file; Spark Open rated it 25%.
Logic-heavy change in source file; Spark Open rated it 12%.
Marked lines merely preserve original IsClosed->OpenedInlines push logic inside null-check; no new branching or state mutation introduced there.

Marked deletion removes the `if (container.IsClosed) InsertAfter` branch; new code always AppendChild when nextInline!=null, so inlines after a closed container will be nested incorrectly and tree structure will be wrong.

Else branch fires when no inline was created (nextInline==null) but sets inlineState.Inline to container.LastChild when it is a LeafInline; a LeafInline is not a valid container/position for subsequent inserts and can corrupt nesting or cause null-parent/cast errors on the next char.

Else branch when nextInline==null now recomputes deepest open container and reassigns inlineState.Inline to LastChild/container instead of leaving it, and deepens only through !IsClosed containers, changing AppendChild vs InsertAfter logic which can misplace subsequent inlines or loop.
Debug trace Log.WriteLine/DumpTo left in hot inline-parsing loop inside marked region will execute on every char and can NPE/crash or flood output if Log is null/disabled in production.

diff.text: inlineState.Inline = container.LastChild is LeafInline ? container.LastChild : container;

reasons.detail: else-branch (nextInline==null) reassigns inlineState.Inline to container.LastChild/container, which was never done before and can cause re-processing of an already-appended leaf, infinite loop, or wrong deepest-container selection instead of advancing the parser cursor.

- [**JIRA links**](src/Markdig.Tests/Specs/JiraLinks.md) to automatically generate links for JIRA project references (Thanks to @clarkd: https://github.com/clarkd/MarkdigJiraLinker)

- [**CJK-friendly Emphasis**](src/Markdig.Tests/Specs/CJKFriendlyEmphasis.md) to mitigate a CommonMark specification issue in CJK languages (Thanks to @tats-u: https://github.com/tats-u/markdown-cjk-friendly)
- Starting with Markdig version `0.20.0+`, Markdig is compatible only with `NETStandard 2.0`, `NETStandard 2.1`, `NETCoreApp 2.1` and `NETCoreApp 3.1`.
If you are looking for support for an old .NET Framework 3.5 or 4.0, you can download Markdig `0.18.3`.

prs.title: Tweaks to the Wondrous calendar system
prs.taskSummary:
Tweaks to the Wondrous calendar system

- Remove WondrousYearInfo: we never need both parts together,
  so just use two separate methods instead.
- Remove the cache: a dictionary is going to be more involved
  than the simple array lookup anyway, and it's not thread-safe.
- Simplify CalculateStartOfYearDays - aside from anything else,
  now we don't need to use DateTime :)
- Change WondrousYearMonthDayCalculator to *only* use the
  "Ayyam-i-Ha are part of month 18" model, e.g. for GetDaysInMonth.
  The alternative model of "Ayyam-i-Ha are in month 0" is used
  extensively in WondrousCalendarSy

diff.text: private const int WondrousMaxYear = 1000; // current lookup tables are pre-calculated for a thousand years
///     There are 19 months in a year. Between the 18th and 19th month are the "days of Ha" (Ayyam-i-Ha).
///     - treat Ayyam-i-Ha as month 0. This will cause problems if 0 is treated as unknown. When stored internally,
///       NodaTime months are converted to 0-based numbers, so this would by -1 which is not supported.
///     - treat Ayyam-i-Ha as month -1. This would be a problem if the base classes convert to 0 based months
///     - treat Ayyam-i-Ha as month 19. This is confusing because the 19th month would be displayed as month #20.
///     - treat Ayyam-i-Ha as month 20. This will cause problems if months are sorted naively.
///     - treat Ayyam-i-Ha as extra days in month 18. This would require special handling to sometimes display
///       days in "month 18" as being Ayyam-i-Ha, but we have no direct control over display.
/// This version will treat Ayyam-i-Ha days as extra days in month 18.
/// Users interacting with the system should use 0 as Ayyam-i-Ha.
/// This is the base64 representation of information for years 172 to 1000.
/// For each year, the value in the array is (NawRuzDate - 19) + 10 * (DaysInAyyamiHa - 4)

reasons.detail: Loop uses accumulated >= offset so a split requested in the middle of a 2-cell CJK character overshoots by 1 cell and includes the whole character, so First.CellCount can exceed offset and a split inside the final character yields an empty string Second instead of null/padding.

Accumulated >= offset includes a double-width char that straddles the split (e.g. width 2 char at offset 1 makes first segment width 2 > offset) and iterates by char not Rune so surrogate pairs/emoji are split incorrectly; correct is to stop before the char that would exceed offset.
